insights.title: More very hot days
insights.body: Days at 35 °C or hotter went from about 4 to 8 a year. Heat at flowering cuts yields of rice, maize and most pulses.

insights.title: Rainfall has increased
insights.body: Yearly rain went from about 2431 mm to 2521 mm.

outlook.method: Theil-Sen trend + Mann-Kendall test on 2001-2024 yearly data, extended to 2035 with an 80% prediction range. Where there is no clear trend, the 2001-2024 average is projected. Statistical extrapolation, not a climate-model forecast.

consequences.headline: Pigeon pea fits 3 points worse by 2035
consequences.detail: If today's trends continue: Pigeon pea 53 → 50 (crop match out of 100).
consequences.action: Build the rotation around crops whose match holds up.

consequences.headline: +0.6 °C warmer on average by 2035
consequences.detail: The yearly average moves from 26.6 °C to about 27.2 °C. Most recommended crops stay inside their temperature range.
consequences.action: Watch heat stress in cool-climate crops; earlier sowing helps.

consequences.headline: About 17% more rain by 2035
consequences.detail: Yearly rain trends from about 2,521 mm to 2,956 mm. More water, but also more waterlogging on heavy soil.
consequences.action: Keep drains open; raised beds help crops that hate wet feet.
